Architecture Diagram

The target is a server-rendered catalog application with MVC presentation, application services, and an Entity Framework persistence layer. It runs in IIS on .NET Framework and can use SQL Server and Azure services, while mock implementations are enabled by default.

Data Storage & External Services

The application persists catalog data through EF6 to SQL Server when mock mode is disabled; the default configuration uses mock catalog data. Images use a mock implementation by default and can use Azure Blob Storage. Microsoft Entra ID, Azure Key Vault configuration, and Application Insights are optional integrations. No active message-broker or distributed-cache usage was identified.

Key Architectural Decisions

  • The MVC application is a single deployable web application with interface-based catalog and image services.
  • Autofac selects mock or production-oriented implementations from configuration.
  • Catalog persistence uses an EF6 context directly; there is no separate repository layer.

DTOs & Contracts

CatalogItem, CatalogBrand, and CatalogType are mutable EF entity classes; CatalogItem is also used as the MVC form-binding type. PaginatedItemsViewModel is the catalog-list response model. Image upload returns an anonymous JSON response with a name and URL. No immutable API DTOs, gateway aggregation DTOs, explicit serialization customization, or API specification was found.

Communication Patterns

Controller-to-service communication is synchronous and in-process through ICatalogService and IImageService. The database service uses EF6 over SQL Server; Azure image storage is optional and is called directly from the MVC process. No asynchronous message broker flow, API gateway, service discovery, retry policy, circuit breaker, or client-side load balancing was found. Startup initializes Autofac and routes, conditionally initializes the SQL database, initializes catalog images, and configures telemetry.

Authentication is configuration-dependent: Microsoft Entra ID OpenID Connect and cookies are enabled only when the corresponding feature flag is true; otherwise a custom OWIN middleware supplies a claims identity. Catalog mutations have [Authorize] attributes, but no role-based policy was found. The Docker port mapping exposes the application container’s HTTP port; no application-level TLS enforcement was identified.

  4. Image initialization runs during startup; telemetry initialization is added before request processing.

Core Business Workflows

The application supports maintaining and browsing an e-commerce product catalog. Catalog staff can create, edit, and remove products, while visitors browse products and view details; product imagery is handled through a separate image service.

Domain Entities

EntityService / Bounded ContextDescriptionKey Relationships
CatalogItemeShopModernizedMVC / Product CatalogA product offered in the catalog with price, stock, and image metadataBelongs to one catalog brand and one catalog type
CatalogBrandeShopModernizedMVC / Product CatalogBrand classification for productsCan classify multiple catalog items
CatalogTypeeShopModernizedMVC / Product CatalogCategory/type classification for productsCan categorize multiple catalog items

Service-to-Domain Mapping

ServiceDomain ContextOwned EntitiesExternal Dependencies
eShopModernizedMVCProduct CatalogCatalogItem, CatalogBrand, CatalogTypeSQL Server when database mode is enabled; optional Azure Blob Storage
CatalogServiceMockProduct Catalog (development/mock)In-memory CatalogItem listPreconfigured in-process data
Image serviceCatalog mediaImage metadata/URL only; bytes are outside the catalog database in Azure modeAzure Blob Storage or mock local image paths

All domain operations occur in one application. There are no separate bounded-context services, cross-service events, or distributed data exchanges.

Primary Workflows

Workflow 1: Browse the catalog

  1. A visitor opens GET /Catalog/Index, optionally supplying pageSize and pageIndex.
  2. CatalogController asks ICatalogService for an ordered catalog page with associated brand and type data.
  3. The selected database-backed or mock service returns a paginated view model.
  4. The controller builds the image URLs and renders the catalog view.

Workflow 2: Create or update a catalog item

  1. An authorized catalog user opens the create or edit form and submits a CatalogItem.
  2. MVC model validation checks the entity; invalid values return the form with validation state.
  3. The service persists the item through EF6 and assigns an application-generated identifier for new items.
  4. When a temporary image is present, the image service promotes it to the item’s final image location.
  5. The user is redirected to the catalog listing.

Workflow 3: Upload a catalog image

  1. The browser posts an image and item identifier to /uploadimage.
  2. PicController attempts to decode the input as an image and accepts JPEG, PNG, or GIF formats.
  3. The configured image service stores the image in Azure Blob Storage or uses the mock implementation.
  4. The controller returns a JSON object with the image URL and name for the form workflow.

Workflow 4: Remove a catalog item

  1. An authorized user opens the delete confirmation for a catalog item.
  2. The POST delete action resolves the item through ICatalogService, removes it, and redirects to the catalog.

Cross-Service Data Flows

No service-to-service data composition exists. The MVC application reads and writes catalog entities through its own EF context. When Azure storage is enabled, image operations are a direct application-to-Blob interaction; there is no downstream service fallback policy. The mock image implementation returns local image URLs instead of performing a remote upload.

sequenceDiagram participant Staff as "Catalog Staff" participant Browser as "Browser" participant Controller as "CatalogController" participant Service as "CatalogService" participant Generator as "HiLo ID Generator" participant DB as "SQL Server" participant Image as "Image Service" Staff->>Browser: Submit new catalog item Browser->>Controller: POST /Catalog/Create Controller->>Controller: Validate CatalogItem model alt Validation fails Controller-->>Browser: Re-render form with validation errors else Validation succeeds Controller->>Service: CreateCatalogItem(item) Service->>Generator: Allocate catalog ID Generator->>DB: Read next sequence value when needed DB-->>Generator: Sequence value Generator-->>Service: Catalog ID Service->>DB: Insert catalog item DB-->>Service: Save completed opt Temporary image supplied Controller->>Image: Promote temporary image Image-->>Controller: Image operation completed end Controller-->>Browser: Redirect to catalog end Browser-->>Staff: Show updated catalog

Business Rules & Decision Logic

  • A catalog item requires a name; price is constrained to 0 through 1,000,000 and at most two decimal places.
  • Available stock, restock threshold, and maximum stock threshold are constrained to 0 through 10,000,000.
  • Catalog items require a valid brand and type relationship.
  • New database-backed catalog items use a Hi-Lo sequence generator; mock items receive an identifier based on the current in-memory list.
  • Image upload accepts decoded JPEG, PNG, and GIF formats. Image storage behavior is selected by configuration.
  • Create, edit, and delete catalog actions are marked [Authorize]; reads and image upload are not marked with that attribute.
  • No order, payment, checkout, inventory reservation, audit-trail, or multi-service transaction workflow was found.

Version & Compatibility Risks

The application remains on .NET Framework 4.7.2, ASP.NET MVC 5, and EF6, which require Windows hosting and have a migration path to modern .NET rather than a direct framework retarget. The CVE scan found medium-severity advisories affecting log4net 2.0.12 and IdentityModel packages 5.6.0; see the security assessment for the affected package ranges.

Notable Observations

  • packages.config contains 146 package entries, including many transitive System.* and Microsoft support packages.
  • Redis and Azure Service Bus packages are present, but corresponding active application usage was not found; the Redis session block is commented out.
  • System.Data.SqlClient is used by the application but is provided as a framework reference, not a package entry.
  • No test framework dependencies or test project were found in the target solution.

Data Architecture & Persistence Layer

The catalog data model contains three EF6 entities stored in SQL Server when the database-backed mode is enabled. The application also supports a default in-memory catalog mock and optional image storage outside the relational database.

Entity Model

erDiagram CatalogBrand ||--o{ CatalogItem : "brands" CatalogType ||--o{ CatalogItem : "categorizes" CatalogBrand { int Id PK string Brand } CatalogType { int Id PK string Type } CatalogItem { int Id PK string Name string Description decimal Price string PictureFileName int CatalogBrandId FK int CatalogTypeId FK int AvailableStock int RestockThreshold int MaxStockThreshold bool OnReorder }

CatalogItem is the central catalog entity and has required foreign-key relationships to CatalogBrand and CatalogType. The EF context maps these to the Catalog, CatalogBrand, and CatalogType tables; the item identifier is generated by an application-side Hi-Lo sequence mechanism.

The mock service implements the same interface against a shared in-memory list. The relational service uses EF DbSet operations and SaveChanges; no custom SQL repository or stored procedure layer was found beyond the sequence queries used by the ID generator.

Caching Strategy

No application data cache was identified. Redis client and Redis session-state packages are declared, but the Redis session configuration in Web.config is commented out and no active cache provider is registered.

Data Ownership Boundaries

This is a single application and database boundary: the MVC application is the source of truth for catalog items, brands, and types. There is no cross-service database access or service-to-service data composition. Catalog item image bytes are stored in Azure Blob Storage only when Azure storage is enabled; otherwise the mock image service returns local image URLs. Mock catalog mode uses a process-wide in-memory list rather than a persistent store.
